paper.title_en: Isomeric states in odd-<math><mi>A</mi></math> tantalum isotopes with <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>106</mn><mo>–</mo><mn>116</mn></mrow></math>
paper.abstract_en: The structure of high-<math><mi>K</mi></math> isomeric states in the odd-<math><mi>A</mi></math> tantalum <math><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>73</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> isotopes is investigated systematically within the cranked Nilsson–Strutinsky (CNS) and cranked Nilsson–Strutinsky–Bogoliubov (CNSB) frameworks, spanning neutron numbers <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>106</mn><mo>–</mo><mn>116</mn></mrow></math>. The low-lying one-proton isomers are identified with the <math><mrow><mn>9</mn><mo>/</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo></msup><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>514</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></math>, <math><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>/</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo></msup><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>402</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></math>, and <math><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo></msup><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>411</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></math> Nilsson orbitals, while the two-quasineutron configurations <math><mrow><msup><mi>K</mi><mi>π</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>8</mn><mo>−</mo></msup></mrow></math>, <math><msup><mn>10</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></math>, and <math><msup><mn>10</mn><mo>−</mo></msup></math> are shown to play a decisive role in driving multiquasiparticle isomer formation across the chain. High-<math><mi>K</mi></math> isomers are predicted in <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Ta</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>189</mn></mmultiscripts></math> at low excitation energies, presenting a strong motivation for future experiments. The CNSB calculations predict a transition from stable prolate shapes to triaxiality and shape coexistence in odd-<math><mi>A</mi></math> Ta isotopes near <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>–</mo><mn>116</mn></mrow></math>.
